idiom_name: callback-slot table: struct of function pointers plus void* context (GObject-signals shape)
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the Mediator collapses into a hub struct that owns a table of slots - one function pointer plus an opaque void* context per colleague - and one dispatch entry point; colleagues register their callbacks and call emit(hub, sender, event) instead of calling each other. GLib's GObject signals are the library-grade version of exactly this shape: g_signal_connect() attaches a GCallback plus user data to a named signal on an object instance, and g_signal_emit() calls the handlers synchronously and does not return until all of them have run. Write the table by hand when the GLib dependency is not an option; the structure is the same, with less lifetime bookkeeping done for you.
pitfalls: A function pointer plus void* context is the only closure C has, so a wrong or freed context is undetected: the hub holds raw pointers with no type or lifetime check, and a colleague must unregister before it is destroyed.

GObject does not disconnect g_signal_connect() handlers automatically; only g_signal_connect_object() ties the handler's lifetime to another object, and its documentation notes that it is not thread-safe.
A handler that emits or unregisters while the table is being dispatched mutates it mid-iteration; define the re-entrancy rule and iterate over a snapshot when handlers may unsubscribe.
